content.text:
I read the code. **Line references are accurate** — I spot-checked every one (`TerminalSessions.swift:400/409-413/518/525`, `AppStore.swift:3454-3482/3493/3502/3515/3671/3723/3703/996/156-177/828`, `ChangesetDetailView.swift:28-32/311`, `TitlebarBars.swift:113-129`, `TabContent` at 100-122). The root-cause diagnosis is right. The problems are design-level.

---

## 1. ⌘D on a diff pane creates twin tabs with identical content identity — step 2 is nondeterministic and lands in the wrong pane

`TerminalSessions.newPaneTab` (`:692-710`) **deliberately** builds a duplicate content tab: "Built directly (not via `openDiffPreview`) so the same-file dedup doesn't collapse it back onto the anchor." Same for `.changeset`. So the invariant step 2 silently relies on — at most one tab per (target, content identity) — is false by design.

`contentTab(matching:)` (`:441`) is `tabsByTarget[target]?.first { … }` over an **unordered dictionary**. Reachable failure:

1. Preview `T1` shows `Gemfile` → entry `(T1, Gemfile)`.
2. ⌘D the diff pane → `newPaneTab` persists `T1`, spawns preview `T2` also showing `Gemfile`, focuses it → entry `(T2, Gemfile)`.
3. Click `user.rb` → retargets `T2` → entry `(T2, user.rb)`.
4. Back → recorded `(T2, Gemfile)`; `T2` exists but mismatches → step 2 → `openContentPreview(Gemfile)` → Inv C dedup matches **either twin**. If it picks `T1` (the pinned one), focus jumps to the pinned pane and `T2` — the pane you were browsing in — still shows `user.rb`. Back visibly did the wrong thing, ~50% of the time.

This is exactly the scenario the plan's **test 5** ("Cmd-D twin panes, Back to the anchor entry, tab count unchanged") claims to cover. As written it will be flaky and it asserts the wrong invariant (tab count) instead of the one that breaks (which pane got the content). Step 2 must prefer `loc.tab` when it exists, or `openContentPreview` needs a deterministic tie-break — neither is in the plan.

## 2. The design builds the machinery to survive a tab close, then out-of-scopes using it

Plan: "relaxing prune/isLive so content entries outlive their tab" — out of scope. Test 9 actively pins the current behaviour.

But `onTabsRemoved` → `history.prune(removing:)` drops every entry whose `tab` id is gone. All your file-browsing entries name the **one shared preview slot**. So: browse `Gemfile → user.rb → README` in the preview, then ⌘W that tab → **all three entries die, `canGoBack` goes false, your entire browsing history is erased by one keystroke.** That is the single most common way to leave a preview tab.

Step 2's spawn branch (plan's own test 10) proves a content entry is fully reconstructible without its tab. Once content is in the location, tab-id is the wrong liveness key for `.diff`/`.file`/`.changeset` — `isLive` should be "target is live", and `prune` should only drop `.terminal` entries. That deletes the "prune asymmetry" the plan instead chooses to *document and pin with a test*. Documenting incoherence you have the machinery to fix is the wrong call.

## 3. Step 1 is near-dead code; 3 of the 5 fire sites are dead

The plan's own framing: "Content identity is mutated in exactly two places: the retarget at `:410` and `setChangesetSelectedPath` at `:525`." Two bullets later it fires the seam from **five** places.

Trace them:
- `openContentPreview` Inv C dedup branch: content unmodified. Either `focus` changed → `onFocusChange` already recorded, or nothing changed → nothing to record. Dead.
- `openContentPreview` spawn branch: `setFocused` on a brand-new tab always fires `onFocusChange` (it can't already be focused). Dead.
- `openContentPersistent` both branches: dedup promotes preview→persisted, which `isPreview` normalisation erases; new-tab branch is `setFocused` again. Dead — and **test 13 exists to verify dead code dedups.**
- Only the **retarget** branch (`:409-413`) and `setChangesetSelectedPath` genuinely need it.

Five fire sites means five paths the AppStore-side guard must be right about instead of two, and it makes the seam mean "an open happened" rather than "content identity changed" — which is why the guard becomes load-bearing at all.

Step 1 is likewise redundant with step 2's Inv C branch **except** in the twin-pane case from §1 — which the plan doesn't know about, so it justifies step 1 on grounds that don't hold and omits the one reason it's needed.

## 4. "Step 2 opens into the PREVIEW SLOT" is wrong in the reachable case — Back can create a tab

Plan: "when the recorded tab was pinned and drifted, step 2 opens into the PREVIEW SLOT and leaves the pinned tab untouched."

A pinned tab cannot drift — `openContentPreview` only retargets `previewTabID`. The reachable path is drift-**then**-pin: preview `T`→`Gemfile` (entry), `T`→`user.rb` (entry), then Keep Open `T`. Now `previewTabID` is `nil`. Back → no tab matches `Gemfile`, no preview slot → **spawn**. Tab count goes 1→2. The user gained a permanent tab by pressing Back, and it isn't recorded, so the tab count ratchets in a way nothing cleans up.

That directly contradicts the plan's UITest assertion "pane count is still 1" as a general invariant, and it's a UX decision (should Back mutate tab structure?) the plan never raises. Same path is reachable via ⌘D (`newPaneTab` persists "any other preview").

## 5. `NavContent` re-implements `FocusedTabSelection`, and adds 5 exhaustive switches for a guarantee already held 4×

`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift` is already an `Equatable`, identity-only reduction of `TabContent` — `.diff(path, source)`, `.file(path)`, `.changeset(commitID)`, `.terminal → nil` — with the *same* documented rationale ("a new `TabContent` case has exactly one site to teach"). Its identity fields are byte-for-byte what the plan specifies for `NavContent`'s hand-written `==`.

The plan adds a second parallel enum with **five** new exhaustive switches (`init`, hand-written `==` with 8 arms, `matchesTab`, `openAsPreview`, `reapplyNonIdentity`). `TabContent.filePath`, `FocusedTabSelection.current`, `persist`, and the renderer already make a 5th kind a compile error four times over. The plan's central design justification — "so a 5th `TabContent` kind is a compile error" — buys nothing that isn't already bought, at the cost of two enums that can silently disagree.

Simpler and strictly better: `NavLocation` holds `contentID: FocusedTabSelection?` (identity, drives derived `==`) plus an opaque replay payload excluded from `==`. `==` collapses from 8 hand-written arms to one line. Combined with §2 (drop `tab` from content-entry identity) and §3 (2 fire sites), and step 2 becomes the whole of replay:

```
.terminal → focus recorded tab
content   → openContentPreview(descriptor)   // Inv C / retarget / spawn already do the right thing
```

No `matchesTab`, no 3-step decision tree, no `reapplyNonIdentity` (redundant in 2 of its 3 branches anyway — `openContentPreview` writes `selectedPath` into the descriptor in the retarget and spawn branches), no ASCII decision tree, no prune-asymmetry doc + test.

## 6. Replay reinstates a stale `DiffDescriptor.change` into live UI

The plan cites `change` drift as the reason to exclude it from `==`, then never notes that step 2 writes the **record-time** value back into a rendered tab. `change` is not inert:
- `DiffViewer.swift:157-159` — the change-kind letter and its colour.
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:293/872/878` — `.disabled(descriptor.change == .deleted)` on "Open file in…".

Record a `.modified` diff, delete the file, press Back: badge says `M`, and "Open file in editor" is **enabled** for a file that no longer exists. Inverse case wrongly disables it. Either re-resolve `change` from live status on replay, or drop it from the payload and have the viewer resolve it.

## 7. Replaying a working-tree diff that is no longer a change is unspecified

Today the only content ever replayed is a `.changeset` — an immutable commit. Extending replay to `.diff(source: .gitWorktree/.jjWorkingCopy)` and `.file` introduces a new class of dead location: Back to a diff for a file you've since reverted, or a file you've deleted. The plan says nothing about what the pane shows. Nothing in `isLive` catches it (the target is alive). A browser shows a 404 deliberately; this will show whatever `DiffResolver`/`PlainFileViewer` happen to do with a missing input. Needs an explicit decision, and it's the most likely source of a "Back is broken" bug report post-ship.

## 8. The seam-wiring bullet omits `!isNavigatingHistory`

`recordCurrentLocation()` does **not** self-guard — its doc says "No-op while replaying (guarded at the call sites)", and every existing caller (`:162`, `:837`, `:3493`, `:3502`, `:3514`) carries the check. The plan's §3 wiring bullet lists only the target/tab guards. Given the plan is line-precise everywhere else, and given `withHistorySuppressed` exists *specifically* so this guard works under nesting, leaving it out of the one bullet that establishes the new record path is a spec hole an implementer will hit as "replay records itself."

## 9. The UITest drives a surface no UITest has ever driven

`toolbar.toggleSidebar` and `toolbar.quickTerminal` already exist as identifiers. **Zero UITests reference either.** The nav chevrons live in an `NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController`-hosted `NSHostingView` (`TitlebarAccessoryHost.swift:53-56`). SwiftUI `Button`s in a titlebar accessory routinely don't surface under `app.buttons` in the main window's tree without extra coaxing, and they're `.disabled(!store.canGoBack)` so a naive `.tap()` silently no-ops.

The proven idiom in this repo is `app.typeKey("[", modifierFlags: .command)` (`ViewMenuShortcutsUITests`), and `Go ▸ Back` with `.keyboardShortcut("[", .command)` already exists (`WorkroomApp.swift:1129`), reserved from the terminal via `isAppShortcut`. The focused pane in the test is a diff pane, so nothing swallows it. Add the identifiers if you want them, but don't make the only end-to-end coverage of this fix depend on an unvalidated accessibility path.

Also: the plan says run via "direct `xcodebuild -only-testing`" *and* that the new file needs `xcodegen generate`. A direct `xcodebuild` skips xcodegen, so that's `make app-generate` first. And the three new **unit** test files need the same regeneration — `make app-test` handles it, but the plan only flags xcodegen for the UITest, implying otherwise.

## 10. Out-of-scoping `activeInspectorSection` leaves the reported symptom half-fixed

The complaint is "Back moves the sidebar but not the pane." After this plan, Back from a changeset to a diff reinstates the diff pane, moves the sidebar, and leaves the inspector showing **History** — no row highlighted, because `FocusedTabSelection.current` now returns `.diff` and no History row matches. Back still looks broken to the person who filed it.

The fix is one `@Published` field (`AppStore.swift:439`) and a three-case mapping (`.diff`/`.file` → `.changes`, `.changeset` → `.history`), plus a `Defaults` write to suppress under replay. That is cheaper than several of the 24 tests being added. Deferring it is the wrong prioritisation.

## 11. Test budget is miscalibrated

7 pure + 13 store + 3 sessions + 1 UI = **24 new tests** for ~150 lines of production change. Of those, test 13 covers dead code (§3), the prune-asymmetry test pins behaviour that §2 argues should change, test 5 is flaky as specified (§1), and test 4 asserts an outcome the plan describes wrongly (§4). Cut the fire sites to 2 and the decision tree to 2 branches and roughly half of these stop having anything to assert.

---

### Minor
- `prune`'s adjacent-dup collapse and `record`'s dedup now run on the identity-only `==`, so collapsing two entries with the same identity but different payloads keeps the **older** payload. Harmless, but it's another reason the payload shouldn't carry live-rendered fields (§6).
- `selectChangesetFile` today has no selected-target guard, so a file tap in a co-displayed non-selected pane records against the *selected* target's focused tab — a wrong-tab entry. Moving to the seam + the plan's guard silently fixes this; the plan never says so, and test 8 asserts the new behaviour without arguing it (should the tap instead promote focus, as `select` does?).
- `previewTabID` is also `.first` over an unordered dictionary; combined with `newPaneTab` persisting "any other preview", the ≤1-preview invariant is what keeps it deterministic. Worth a note since replay now depends on it.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/NavigationHistory.swift
- /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift

**Why Codex kept timing out — three different causes, only the last one a real timeout:**

1. **First run failed, didn't time out.** The command sandbox blocked its IPC: `failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Operation not permitted (os error 1)`. Codex needs to spawn a local app-server socket, which the sandbox denies.
2. **Second run sat idle waiting for input.** `$TMPDIR` differs between a sandboxed and an unsandboxed shell, so the prompt file I'd staged wasn't there — `cat` returned nothing, Codex got an empty prompt and printed "What would you like help with?" until the clock ran out. My error.
3. **Third run was a genuine timeout.** `model_reasoning_effort="high"` on gpt-5.6-sol, reading ~12 Swift files with a 9KB prompt, exceeded the skill's hard 5-minute cap (`timeout: 300000`). Nothing broke; it just needed longer.

If you want Codex specifically, the fixes are: drop to `medium` reasoning, narrow the file list, and run it with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`. Say the word and I'll re-run it with a 10-minute budget. The fallback ran instead, and it was worth it.

## OUTSIDE VOICE (Claude subagent)

Codex timed out, so this is a fresh-context Claude subagent. It confirmed every line reference in the plan, then found eleven things the review missed. I verified its five load-bearing claims against the code myself — all five hold.

**§5 — VERIFIED, and it invalidates my finding 3. `FocusedTabSelection` already IS the identity type `NavContent` was going to re-implement.**
```swift
// FocusedTabSelection.swift:22-24 — byte-for-byte the identity fields I specified for NavContent.==
case changeset(commitID: String)
case diff(path: String, source: DiffSource)
case file(path: String)
```
It is already `Equatable`, already has the one exhaustive switch (`current(store:sessions:)`), and its doc already claims the same guarantee: *"a new `TabContent` case has exactly one site to teach."* The plan adds a second parallel enum with **five** new exhaustive switches to buy a guarantee this type already provides. My finding 3 was solving a problem that shouldn't exist.

**§1 — VERIFIED. Twin tabs with identical content identity are by design, so replay's dedup is nondeterministic.**
```swift
// TerminalSessions.swift:689-690 — newPaneTab's own comment
/// Built directly (not via `openDiffPreview`) so the same-file dedup doesn't collapse it back onto the anchor.
```
`contentTab(matching:)` is `.first` over an unordered dictionary. After ⌘D, Back can focus the pinned twin instead of the pane you were browsing — roughly a coin flip. The plan's test 5 asserts tab count, not which pane got the content, so it would pass while the bug ships.

**§6 — VERIFIED. Replay writes a record-time `change` into live UI.**
```swift
DiffViewer.swift:157   Text(Self.changeLetter(descriptor.change))
TerminalTabStrip.swift:293/872/878   .disabled(descriptor.change == .deleted)
```
Record a `.modified` diff, delete the file, press Back: badge shows `M` and "Open file in…" is enabled for a file that's gone.

**§8 — VERIFIED. `recordCurrentLocation:3661` has no self-guard** ("guarded at the call sites"), and my seam-wiring bullet omitted `!isNavigatingHistory`. Spec hole; folding the fix in.

**§9 — VERIFIED. Zero UITests drive any `toolbar.*` identifier**; `typeKey` is the idiom in 10+ UITest files. The chevrons live in an `NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController`-hosted `NSHostingView` and are `.disabled` when history is empty, so a naive `.tap()` can silently no-op.

Also raised: §3 three of five seam fire sites are dead code (test 13 would test dead code), §4 Back can create a tab via drift-then-pin, §7 replaying a diff for a reverted file is unspecified, §10 the inspector section isn't restored so the reported symptom stays half-fixed, §11 24 tests for ~150 lines is miscalibrated.

**CROSS-MODEL TENSION**
- **Identity type:** Review said hand-write `NavContent.==` exhaustively (finding 3, you chose 3A). Outside voice says reuse `FocusedTabSelection` and derive `==`. I find the outside voice more compelling — I missed an existing type that does exactly this. Context I might be missing: `NavContent` also has to carry a *replay payload* (the full descriptor), which `FocusedTabSelection` deliberately does not, so this is not a pure swap.
- **prune/isLive:** Outside voice argues for the third time that content entries should outlive their tab. You've now decided this twice (once explicitly, once as 1A). **Your decision stands and I'm not re-asking.** Noted as unresolved-by-design in the report.

questions.question:
5 — Reuse `FocusedTabSelection` as the location identity, or keep the hand-written `NavContent`? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-navcontent-vs-focusedtabselection>

Project/branch/task: `workroom` on `master`; back/forward detail-pane fix, cross-model tension.

ELI10: A history entry needs two different things from the pane it recorded. It needs an *identity* — just enough to answer "is this the same place?" so Back does not pile up duplicates — and it needs a *payload*, the full descriptor, so replay can actually re-open the thing. My plan built one new type to do both jobs, which forced the identity comparison to be hand-written, because the payload contains fields that drift. The outside voice found that the identity half already exists: `FocusedTabSelection` reduces a pane to exactly path-plus-source, path, or commit-id, is already `Equatable`, and already carries the doc promise that a new pane kind has one place to teach. So the honest move is to keep the payload and stop re-deriving the identity.

Stakes if we pick wrong: keep two parallel enums and they can silently disagree — the inspector highlights one row while history thinks you are somewhere else, which is a nastier version of the bug being fixed. Reuse it and the risk moves elsewhere: `FocusedTabSelection` is load-bearing for the WORKROOM-2B hang fix, so anything added to it re-enters that hot path, and it has no `.terminal` case (terminals map to `nil`), so a terminal location needs representing some other way.

Recommendation: A, because you flag repetition aggressively and this is the clearest DRY hit in the whole plan — one type owning identity, the payload alongside it and excluded from equality, and `==` collapsing from eight hand-written arms to derived.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=6/10

Pros / cons:
5A) Identity is `FocusedTabSelection?`; payload is a separate field excluded from `==` (recommended)
  ✅ Removes a whole parallel enum and five exhaustive switches, and makes it structurally impossible for the row highlight and history to disagree about what "same place" means
  ✅ `==` becomes derived instead of eight hand-written arms, which also retires finding 3 entirely and drops several of the tests that only existed to police those arms (human: ~3h / CC: ~15 min)
  ❌ `FocusedTabSelection` has no terminal case, so a terminal entry needs an explicit representation, and touching a type that is load-bearing for the App Hang fix demands care that a brand-new type would not
5B) Keep the hand-written `NavContent` as planned in 3A
  ✅ Leaves `FocusedTabSelection` completely untouched, so the WORKROOM-2B hot path cannot regress from this change at all

6 — Replay writes a record-time `DiffDescriptor.change` back into live UI. Fix it, or accept it? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-stale-change-field>

Project/branch/task: `workroom` on `master`; back/forward detail-pane fix, correctness finding from the outside voice.

ELI10: A diff tab carries a `change` field saying whether the file was added, modified, or deleted. It is not decoration — `DiffViewer.swift:157` paints it as a coloured letter in the header, and `TerminalTabStrip.swift:293/872/878` uses it to enable or disable "Open file in…". The plan snapshots that field into history and writes it back on Back. So: view a modified file, delete it, press Back, and the header still says M while "Open file in…" offers to open a file that no longer exists. To be fair to the plan, an already-open diff tab is stale in exactly the same way today — nothing refreshes `change` on an open tab. Replay does not invent the problem; it stretches the staleness window from "since you opened the tab" to "since some arbitrary earlier point in your session".

Stakes if we pick wrong: accept it and Back can enable a menu item that acts on a deleted file, which at worst is a no-op in the opener but reads as a bug. Fix it in the wrong place and you are refactoring `DiffDescriptor` and every construction site, which is a different change wearing this change's clothes.

Recommendation: A, because the changed-file list the Changes panel already renders is the live answer, looking one path up in it is a handful of lines, and it makes Back strictly more correct than leaving a tab open — without touching `DiffDescriptor` or its callers.

Completeness: A=9/10, B=6/10, C=10/10

Pros / cons:
6A) Re-resolve `change` at replay time from the live changed-file list, falling back to the recorded value (recommended)
  ✅ Fixes the badge and the "Open file in…" enablement at the one moment they can be wrong, using status the app has already fetched and rendered
  ✅ Contained entirely inside replay — `DiffDescriptor`, its construction sites, and the tab strip are untouched (human: ~1h / CC: ~10 min)
  ❌ Replay now depends on status being loaded, so a Back pressed before the first status refresh silently keeps the recorded value — correct, but a second code path to reason about
6B) Accept it; document that replay reproduces open-tab staleness
  ✅ Zero code, and the resulting behaviour is exactly what an open diff tab already does, so nothing becomes inconsistent with the rest of the app
  ✅ Keeps the diff tight around the actual bug being fixed rather than widening into diff-metadata freshness
  ❌ Back can enable an action against a file that is gone, and the staleness window is now unbounded rather than "since you opened it", so the odds of seeing it go up
6C) Remove `change` from `DiffDescriptor`; have the viewer resolve it from live status
  ✅ Fixes the root cause for open tabs and replayed tabs at once, so the badge can never be stale anywhere
  ❌ Touches `DiffDescriptor`, every construction site, and three tab-strip call sites — a separate refactor smuggled into a navigation fix, and it re-enters the row-invalidation hot path

Net: A buys the correct badge and menu state for ten minutes of work; C is the real root-cause fix and belongs in its own change.

options.description: At replay, look the path up in the live changed-file list and use its current change kind; fall back to the recorded value if status isn't loaded. DiffDescriptor untouched.

options.label: 6B Accept and document
options.description: Replay writes the recorded value, matching what an already-open diff tab does today. Zero code; note it on the payload field.

options.label: 6C Remove change from DiffDescriptor

content.text:
Rule taken. That's cleaner than what I had, and it settles three open threads at once.

**What it changes:**

- **Replay's spawn branch dies.** The plan (and the outside voice's §4) had Back creating a tab when the recorded content had nowhere to go. Forbidden now.
- **Resolution becomes four ordered steps, none of which create anything:** recorded tab still shows it → focus it; else another live tab shows it → focus that; else the shared preview slot exists → retarget it in place (this is not reopening — that tab is open, and retargeting is exactly what browsing does, so the core fix still works); else **the entry is unreachable → Back skips it and keeps stepping.**
- **`isLive` gains a content-reachability check** — cheap and synchronous (does a tab match, or does a preview slot exist?), no VCS I/O. This is the mechanism that makes "ignore what was closed" work: `step(_:isLive:)` already skips dead entries.
- **Two decisions get superseded, both toward simpler:** your Keep-Open answer ("open in the preview slot") now applies *only when a preview slot exists* — with everything pinned, Back skips instead of spawning. And the outside voice's repeated argument that content entries should outlive their tab is now definitively rejected: closed means ignored.
- **Test 10 inverts** — from "replay spawns a tab" to "replay never spawns; the entry is skipped, tab count unchanged."

Two findings still need your call.

7 — How many places fire the new content-change seam? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-seam-fire-sites>

Project/branch/task: `workroom` on `master`; back/forward fix, outside-voice finding §3.

ELI10: The seam is the new notification that says "a tab's content changed, record a history step." My plan fires it from five places. The outside voice says three of those five can never record anything, and I traced it and agree: opening content into a brand-new tab always changes which tab is focused, and the existing focus notification already records that. Same for re-selecting a tab that is already open. Only two places genuinely need the seam — retargeting the shared preview slot in place, and changing which file is selected inside a commit — because those two mutate a tab without moving focus, which is the whole reason this bug exists.

Stakes if we pick wrong: five fire sites means five paths the guard must be right about instead of two, and it quietly redefines the seam from "content identity changed" to "an open happened", which is what made the guard load-bearing in the first place. It also means one planned test exists purely to prove that dead code deduplicates.

Recommendation: A, because the plan's own justification is "content identity is mutated in exactly two places", and firing from five contradicts that sentence. Explicit over clever: the seam should mean exactly what its name says.

Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.

Pros / cons:
7A) Fire from exactly the two real mutation sites (recommended)
  ✅ The seam means precisely "content identity changed", so the guard has two paths to be right about instead of five and the name matches the behaviour
  ✅ Drops the test that only existed to prove dead code deduplicates, and makes the sessions-level tests assert something real (human: ~20 min saved / CC: ~5 min saved)
  ❌ If a future refactor makes one of the three now-silent branches stop firing the focus notification, history goes quiet there with no test to catch it
7B) Fire from all five branches as planned
  ✅ Defensive: any branch that stops firing the focus notification is still covered, and the deduplication absorbs every redundant fire for free
  ✅ No need to reason about which branches change focus — fire everywhere and let one rule sort it out
  ❌ Redefines the seam as "an open happened", which is why the guard became load-bearing, and it ships a test whose only job is to verify unreachable code

Net: A makes the seam mean what it is called; B trades that precision for redundancy the deduplication already provides.

options.label: 7A Two sites (Recommended)
options.description: Fire only from the preview-slot retarget and setChangesetSelectedPath. The other three branches already record via onFocusChange. Drops the double-record test.

options.label: 7B All five as planned
options.description: Fire from all openContentPreview and openContentPersistent branches too; rely on record()'s dedup to absorb the redundant fires.

8 — How should the one end-to-end test drive Back? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-uitest-drive-method>

Project/branch/task: `workroom` on `master`; back/forward fix, outside-voice finding §9.

ELI10: The UI test is the only thing that proves the actual complaint is fixed, because it is the only test that can look at the pane rather than the store. My plan had it click the titlebar back chevron via a new accessibility identifier. The outside voice checked and found that no UI test in this repo has ever driven a titlebar button — two such identifiers already exist and nothing uses them. Those buttons live in an AppKit titlebar accessory hosting a SwiftUI view, which often does not surface in the window's accessibility tree, and they are disabled when history is empty, so a tap that hits nothing fails silently and the test passes for the wrong reason. Meanwhile ten existing UI tests drive shortcuts with a keystroke, and Back already has one.

Stakes if we pick wrong: a silently no-op tap is the worst outcome available here — the test goes green, you believe Back is covered, and the bug can come back untouched. A keystroke either fires or visibly does not.

Recommendation: A, because the keystroke path is proven ten times over in this suite and the menu shortcut already exists and is reserved from the terminal, while the chevron path has zero precedent and a silent-failure mode.

Completeness: A=9/10, B=6/10, C=10/10

Pros / cons:
8A) Drive it with the keystroke; still add the identifiers (recommended)
  ✅ Uses the idiom ten existing UI tests already rely on, against a shortcut that exists and is reserved from the terminal, so the focused diff pane cannot swallow it
  ✅ Keeps the accessibility identifiers as a by-product for future tests and for screen-reader users, at no risk to this test (human: ~1h / CC: ~10 min)
  ❌ Leaves the chevron buttons themselves without end-to-end coverage, so a regression that breaks only the toolbar path would not be caught
8B) Click the chevron via the new accessibility identifier, as planned
  ✅ Tests the control a user actually clicks, and validates the titlebar accessibility path for every future test
  ❌ Zero precedent in this suite, and the specific failure mode is a tap that silently hits nothing — a green test that proves nothing about the bug
8C) Both: keystroke assertion plus a separate chevron test
  ✅ Covers both input routes, so neither the shortcut nor the toolbar can regress unnoticed
  ❌ Doubles the slowest kind of test in the suite, and the chevron half may need real work to make the titlebar accessory queryable at all

Net: A gets trustworthy coverage of the actual fix now; C also covers the button, at the cost of debugging an accessibility path nothing has used.

options.label: 8B Click the chevron
options.description: Tap toolbar.navigateBack as originally planned, accepting that no existing UI test drives a titlebar accessory button.

7 — How many places fire the new content-change seam? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-seam-fire-sites>

Project/branch/task: `workroom` on `master`; back/forward fix, outside-voice finding §3.

ELI10: The seam is the new notification that says "a tab's content changed, record a history step." My plan fires it from five places. The outside voice says three of those five can never record anything, and I traced it and agree: opening content into a brand-new tab always changes which tab is focused, and the existing focus notification already records that. Same for re-selecting a tab that is already open. Only two places genuinely need the seam — retargeting the shared preview slot in place, and changing which file is selected inside a commit — because those two mutate a tab without moving focus, which is the whole reason this bug exists.

Stakes if we pick wrong: five fire sites means five paths the guard must be right about instead of two, and it quietly redefines the seam from "content identity changed" to "an open happened", which is what made the guard load-bearing in the first place. It also means one planned test exists purely to prove that dead code deduplicates.

Recommendation: A, because the plan's own justification is "content identity is mutated in exactly two places", and firing from five contradicts that sentence. Explicit over clever: the seam should mean exactly what its name says.

Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.

Pros / cons:
7A) Fire from exactly the two real mutation sites (recommended)
  ✅ The seam means precisely "content identity changed", so the guard has two paths to be right about instead of five and the name matches the behaviour
  ✅ Drops the test that only existed to prove dead code deduplicates, and makes the sessions-level tests assert something real (human: ~20 min saved / CC: ~5 min saved)
  ❌ If a future refactor makes one of the three now-silent branches stop firing the focus notification, history goes quiet there with no test to catch it

  ✅ Defensive: any branch that stops firing the focus notification is still covered, and the deduplication absorbs every redundant fire for free
  ✅ No need to reason about which branches change focus — fire everywhere and let one rule sort it out
  ❌ Redefines the seam as "an open happened", which is why the guard became load-bearing, and it ships a test whose only job is to verify unreachable code

Net: A makes the seam mean what it is called; B trades that precision for redundancy the deduplication already provides.

options.label: 7B All five as planned
options.description: Fire from all openContentPreview and openContentPersistent branches too; rely on record()'s dedup to absorb the redundant fires.

input.content:
# Back/forward nav must reinstate the detail pane, not just the sidebar

## Context

`⌘[` / the titlebar chevron / Go ▸ Back move the *sidebar/inspector* to the previous item but leave
the detail pane showing what it already showed. Reported as "going back only changes the VCS sidebar
to the previous."

Why, exactly:

- The Changes/Files/History panels share **one preview tab per target**. Clicking a row calls
  `TerminalSessions.openContentPreview` (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:400`), which **retargets that
  tab in place** — same `TerminalTab.ID`, same strip slot (invariant B, `:409-413`).
- Retargeting fires **no focus change** (`focus` early-returns at `:791`, `setFocused` no-ops at
  `:817`), and `AppStore.openDiffPreview` / `openDiffPersistent` / `openFilePreview` /
  `openFilePersistent` (`Core/AppStore.swift:3454-3482`) never call `recordCurrentLocation()`. Only
  the changeset openers (`:3493`, `:3502`) and `selectChangesetFile` (`:3515`) do. So **browsing
  files records no history at all**, and the cursor entry drifts out from under the user.
- `NavLocation` (`Core/NavigationHistory.swift:7`) is `(target, tab)` plus three changeset-shaped
  fields. `AppStore.location(target:tab:)` (`:3671`) captures `.diff` as a bare `filePath` (dropping
  `source: DiffSource` and `change`, both needed to rebuild a `DiffDescriptor`) and captures `.file`
  as **nothing**.
- `applyLocation(_ loc:recordHistory:)` (`:3723`) bails at `guard let commitID = loc.commitID` — so
  **only changesets ever get content reinstated**. The recorded `.diff` `filePath` is dead data.

Chain: `⌘[` steps to an older entry that usually has the *same* `(target, tab)` pair → `focus()`
no-ops → the `commitID` guard returns → the pane is untouched, while `selectedTargetID`'s `didSet`
(`:156-177`) re-points the sidebar. The sidebar row highlight is a derived read of the focused tab
(`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:33`), so it tracks whatever content survives — which is why the
sidebar looks like it moved and the pane didn't.

Only the changeset path was ever wired end to end (`bc762c83`); diff and file tabs stayed on the old
`(target, tab)`-only contract. No test covers content replay: `AppStoreNavigationTests` is
terminal-tabs-only, `NavigationHistoryTests` is pure-value, no UI test drives back/forward.

Outcome: a history entry describes *what was on screen*, not just which tab, and replay reinstates it
for every content kind — so Back walks back through browsed diffs, files, commits, and in-commit file
selections.

## Governing rule (user, this session)

> **Back ignores anything that was closed. Nothing is ever reopened.**

Replay therefore **never creates a tab**. When a recorded location cannot be shown in a tab that
already exists, the entry is unreachable and Back **skips it** and keeps stepping. Retargeting the
shared preview slot is not "reopening" — that tab is open, and retargeting is exactly what browsing
does, which is what makes the core fix work.

## Approach

A recorded location becomes `(target, tab, identity, payload)`. Content mutation gets its own record
seam, because mutating a tab is not a focus change. Replay reinstates content through the existing
`openContentPreview` invariants — no new mutator, and no tab creation.

### 1. `Core/NavigationHistory.swift` — identity reuses `FocusedTabSelection`

`FocusedTabSelection` (`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:18-24`) is **already** the identity-only
reduction of a pane: `.changeset(commitID:)`, `.diff(path:source:)`, `.file(path:)`, terminal ⇒ `nil`.
It is already `Equatable`, and its doc already carries the "a new `TabContent` case has exactly one
site to teach" guarantee. Do not build a parallel enum — reuse it.

```swift
struct NavLocation: Equatable {
  let target: SidebarID
  let tab: TerminalTab.ID
  /// Identity: what makes two locations "the same place". `nil` ⇒ a terminal pane.
  let contentID: FocusedTabSelection?
  /// A changeset's in-commit file selection — identity too, because each selection is its own step.
  /// `FocusedTabSelection.changeset` deliberately carries only the commit id, so this rides alongside.
  let selectedPath: String?
  /// Replay payload — the full descriptor needed to re-open. EXCLUDED from `==`.
  let payload: NavPayload?

  static func == (l: Self, r: Self) -> Bool {
    l.target == r.target && l.tab == r.tab && l.contentID == r.contentID
      && l.selectedPath == r.selectedPath
  }
}

/// The replay payload. Three cases, not four: `TabContent.terminal` holds a live surface, which a
/// value-type history entry must never retain. A terminal location is `payload == nil`.
enum NavPayload { case diff(DiffDescriptor), file(FileDescriptor), changeset(ChangesetDescriptor) }
```

Splitting identity from payload is what removes the hand-written per-kind equality: the drifting
fields (`DiffDescriptor.change` on staging, `ChangesetDescriptor.title` reconstructed on replay,
`isPreview` on Keep Open) live only in `payload`, which `==` never reads — so `record`'s dedup can't
be defeated by drift, and a preview→persist flip is not a new step.

`record` / `step` / `maxEntries` unchanged. `prune(removing:)` unchanged — tab-keyed, so closing a tab
still drops its entries, per the governing rule. Add a doc comment stating the resulting asymmetry
(an entry naming a later-pinned tab survives that tab's close; one naming the preview slot dies with
it) and pin it with a test so it reads as deliberate.

### 2. `Core/TerminalSessions.swift` — one content-change seam, two fire sites

Content identity is mutated in exactly two places (`grep 'tab.content ='`): the retarget at `:410`
and `setChangesetSelectedPath` at `:525`. (`:473-479` is `persist` — `isPreview` only; `:980` is
terminal live state.) Fire the seam from **those two and nowhere else** — the other
`openContentPreview` / `openContentPersistent` branches all end in `setFocused` on a tab that wasn't
focused, so `onFocusChange` already records them. Firing from five sites would redefine the seam as
"an open happened" and ship a test for unreachable code.

- `var onTabContentChange: ((TerminalTarget.ID, TerminalTab.ID) -> Void)?` beside `onFocusChange`
  (`:198`), joining the existing `onTabsRemoved` / `onSurfaceFocused` callbacks.
- An `extension NavPayload` sited directly under `TabContent` (`:101-122`), so a fifth `TabContent`
  case is a compile error in one known place: `init?(_ content: TabContent)` (exhaustive, `isPreview`
  normalised to `false`, `.terminal` ⇒ `nil`), `matchesTab(_:) -> Bool` (delegates to each
  `ContentDescriptor.matches`), and `descriptor` for handing back to the openers.
- **Update the opener ASCII diagram at `:383-389`** to show that every arrow also records a step.
  Without it a reader adds a sixth opener and silently records nothing — this bug's failure mode.

### 3. `Core/AppStore.swift` — record centrally, replay without creating anything

- **`withHistorySuppressed(_:)`** — a save-and-reinstate-prior-value (or depth-counted) replacement
  for the bare `isNavigatingHistory = true; defer { … = false }` pairs at `:3703`, `:3728`, `:996`.
  Today those are two *sequential* windows, which happens to work; wrapping replay in one window
  would let the inner `applyLocation`'s `defer` clear the outer one and replay would record itself.
- **`location(target:tab:)`** (`:3671`) builds identity + payload from `tab.content` via one switch.
- **`applyLocation(_ loc:)`** (`:3723`) — one suppression window, ordered resolution, never creates a
  tab. Drop the dead `recordHistory` parameter (both callers pass `false`). Carries a new ASCII
  decision-tree diagram in its doc comment:

```
  applyLocation(loc)                       // never creates a tab (governing rule)
    │ select loc.target (project + target ids), guard live
    ├── contentID == nil  ─▶ terminal ─▶ focus loc.tab if it still exists ─▶ done
    └── contentID != nil  ─▶ payload must land in an EXISTING tab:
          ├─ 1. loc.tab exists AND payload.matchesTab(its content) ─▶ focus it
          ├─ 2. else some live tab matches payload                 ─▶ focus that tab
          ├─ 3. else the target has a preview slot                 ─▶ retarget it IN PLACE, focus it
          └─ 4. else                        UNREACHABLE ─▶ isLive already rejected it; Back skipped
        then, for the landed tab:
          ├─ .changeset ─▶ setChangesetSelectedPath(loc.selectedPath)
          └─ .diff      ─▶ re-resolve `change` from live status (see below)
```

- **`isLive(_:)`** (`:3746`) gains a content-reachability test, which is the mechanism behind
  "ignore what was closed" — `step(_:isLive:)` already skips entries the predicate rejects:

```swift
  // target alive && !missing, then:
  //   terminal entry  ⟺ loc.tab still exists
  //   content entry   ⟺ some tab matches the payload  ||  the target has a preview slot
```
  Synchronous and cheap — two dictionary walks, no VCS I/O. Deliberately does **not** ask whether the
  file or commit still exists on disk: that needs I/O inside a predicate run per candidate during
  `step`, and the pane already renders its own `.failed` state.

- **Re-resolve `DiffDescriptor.change` on replay.** `change` is not inert — `Views/DiffViewer.swift:157`
  paints it as a coloured letter and `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:293/872/878` gates "Open file in…"
  on `change == .deleted`. Writing a record-time value back would enable that menu item for a file
  that is gone. Look the path up in the live changed-file list the Changes panel already renders and
  use its current `change`; fall back to the recorded value when status isn't loaded yet.
  `DiffDescriptor` and its construction sites are untouched.

- **Wire `terminals.onTabContentChange`** in `init` beside `:828`, guarded on
  `!isNavigatingHistory` **and** `targetID == selectedTarget?.id` **and**
  `tabID == terminals.focusedTab(for: selected)?.id`, then `recordCurrentLocation()`.
  The `!isNavigatingHistory` check is mandatory: `recordCurrentLocation` (`:3661`) does **not**
  self-guard ("guarded at the call sites"), and every existing caller carries it. Do *not* duplicate
  `onFocusChange`'s `fileFind.close()` / `refreshSelectionHasTabs()` — this is not a focus change.

- **Delete** the explicit `recordCurrentLocation()` calls at `:3493`, `:3502`, `:3515` and their
  local guards.

### 4. `Views/ChangesetDetailView.swift:311` — kill a phantom step

`selectedPath` (`:28-32`) falls back to `changeset.files.first?.path` for *display*, so the first row
renders selected while `descriptor.selectedPath == nil`. Tapping it passes `selectChangesetFile`'s
`d.selectedPath != path` guard and records a step whose replay is visually identical. Compare the tap
against the **effective** selection. Pre-existing, same bug class.

### 5. `Views/TitlebarBars.swift:113-129`

Add `.accessibilityIdentifier("toolbar.navigateBack")` / `"toolbar.navigateForward"`, matching the
existing `toolbar.toggleSidebar` convention. The UI test does **not** drive them (see Verification).

| Existing | Used for | Rebuilt? |

| `FocusedTabSelection` (`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:18`) | the location's content identity | **No** — reused; a parallel `NavContent` enum was designed and then deleted from this plan |

# Back/forward nav must reinstate the detail pane, not just the sidebar

## Context

`⌘[` / the titlebar chevron / Go ▸ Back move the *sidebar/inspector* to the previous item but leave
the detail pane showing what it already showed. Reported as "going back only changes the VCS sidebar
to the previous."

Why, exactly:

- The Changes/Files/History panels share **one preview tab per target**. Clicking a row calls
  `TerminalSessions.openContentPreview` (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:400`), which **retargets that
  tab in place** — same `TerminalTab.ID`, same strip slot (invariant B, `:409-413`).
- Retargeting fires **no focus change** (`focus` early-returns at `:791`, `setFocused` no-ops at
  `:817`), and `AppStore.openDiffPreview` / `openDiffPersistent` / `openFilePreview` /
  `openFilePersistent` (`Core/AppStore.swift:3454-3482`) never call `recordCurrentLocation()`. Only
  the changeset openers (`:3493`, `:3502`) and `selectChangesetFile` (`:3515`) do. So **browsing
  files records no history at all**, and the cursor entry drifts out from under the user.
- `NavLocation` (`Core/NavigationHistory.swift:7`) is `(target, tab)` plus three changeset-shaped
  fields. `AppStore.location(target:tab:)` (`:3671`) captures `.diff` as a bare `filePath` (dropping
  `source: DiffSource` and `change`, both needed to rebuild a `DiffDescriptor`) and captures `.file`
  as **nothing**.
- `applyLocation(_ loc:recordHistory:)` (`:3723`) bails at `guard let commitID = loc.commitID` — so
  **only changesets ever get content reinstated**. The recorded `.diff` `filePath` is dead data.

Chain: `⌘[` steps to an older entry that usually has the *same* `(target, tab)` pair → `focus()`
no-ops → the `commitID` guard returns → the pane is untouched, while `selectedTargetID`'s `didSet`
(`:156-177`) re-points the sidebar. The sidebar row highlight is a derived read of the focused tab
(`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:33`), so it tracks whatever content survives — which is why the
sidebar looks like it moved and the pane didn't.

Only the changeset path was ever wired end to end (`bc762c83`); diff and file tabs stayed on the old
`(target, tab)`-only contract. No test covers content replay: `AppStoreNavigationTests` is
terminal-tabs-only, `NavigationHistoryTests` is pure-value, no UI test drives back/forward.

Outcome: a history entry describes *what was on screen*, not just which tab, and replay reinstates it
for every content kind — so Back walks back through browsed diffs, files, commits, and in-commit file
selections.

## Governing rule (user, this session)

> **Back ignores anything that was closed. Nothing is ever reopened.**

Replay therefore **never creates a tab**. When a recorded location cannot be shown in a tab that
already exists, the entry is unreachable and Back **skips it** and keeps stepping. Retargeting the
shared preview slot is not "reopening" — that tab is open, and retargeting is exactly what browsing
does, which is what makes the core fix work.

## Approach

A recorded location becomes `(target, tab, identity, payload)`. Content mutation gets its own record
seam, because mutating a tab is not a focus change. Replay reinstates content through the existing
`openContentPreview` invariants — no new mutator, and no tab creation.

### 1. `Core/NavigationHistory.swift` — identity reuses `FocusedTabSelection`

`FocusedTabSelection` (`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:18-24`) is **already** the identity-only
reduction of a pane: `.changeset(commitID:)`, `.diff(path:source:)`, `.file(path:)`, terminal ⇒ `nil`.
It is already `Equatable`, and its doc already carries the "a new `TabContent` case has exactly one
site to teach" guarantee. Do not build a parallel enum — reuse it.

```swift
struct NavLocation: Equatable {
  let target: SidebarID
  let tab: TerminalTab.ID
  /// Identity: what makes two locations "the same place". `nil` ⇒ a terminal pane.
  let contentID: FocusedTabSelection?
  /// A changeset's in-commit file selection — identity too, because each selection is its own step.
  /// `FocusedTabSelection.changeset` deliberately carries only the commit id, so this rides alongside.
  let selectedPath: String?
  /// Replay payload — the full descriptor needed to re-open. EXCLUDED from `==`.
  let payload: NavPayload?

  static func == (l: Self, r: Self) -> Bool {
    l.target == r.target && l.tab == r.tab && l.contentID == r.contentID
      && l.selectedPath == r.selectedPath
  }
}

/// The replay payload. Three cases, not four: `TabContent.terminal` holds a live surface, which a
/// value-type history entry must never retain. A terminal location is `payload == nil`.
enum NavPayload { case diff(DiffDescriptor), file(FileDescriptor), changeset(ChangesetDescriptor) }
```

be defeated by drift, and a preview→persist flip is not a new step.

176	  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
177	  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
178	  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
179	  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
180	- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
181	  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
182	  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
183	  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.
184	- **⌥Tab / ⌃Tab (the quick switchers, issue #132) are monitor-only and deliberately NOT in
185	  `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut`.** That list is static, but whether the app owns Tab depends on
186	  runtime state: a workroom with one pane has nothing to switch to, so ⌃Tab must reach the TUI. The
187	  monitor branch consumes the event only when a switch actually happened, exactly as ⌥⌘digit and
188	  ⌥⌘arrows already do — same reasoning as the unreserved ⌃⌘arrows. `AppShortcutReservationTests` pins
189	  Tab as never-reserved so a later "defence in depth" edit can't take `<C-Tab>` from every TUI. Both
190	  trigger modifiers are `Defaults` keys (`switcher*Modifier`) because a global-hotkey grabber
191	  (AltTab, HyperSwitch, Contexts all bind ⌥Tab) intercepts upstream of `NSApp.sendEvent`, where no
192	  local monitor can see the key and no API can detect the conflict.

input.plan:
# Back/forward nav must reinstate the detail pane, not just the sidebar

## Context

`⌘[` / the titlebar chevron / Go ▸ Back move the *sidebar/inspector* to the previous item but leave
the detail pane showing what it already showed. Reported as "going back only changes the VCS sidebar
to the previous."

Why, exactly:

- The Changes/Files/History panels share **one preview tab per target**. Clicking a row calls
  `TerminalSessions.openContentPreview` (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:400`), which **retargets that
  tab in place** — same `TerminalTab.ID`, same strip slot (invariant B, `:409-413`).
- Retargeting fires **no focus change** (`focus` early-returns at `:791`, `setFocused` no-ops at
  `:817`), and `AppStore.openDiffPreview` / `openDiffPersistent` / `openFilePreview` /
  `openFilePersistent` (`Core/AppStore.swift:3454-3482`) never call `recordCurrentLocation()`. Only
  the changeset openers (`:3493`, `:3502`) and `selectChangesetFile` (`:3515`) do. So **browsing
  files records no history at all**, and the cursor entry drifts out from under the user.
- `NavLocation` (`Core/NavigationHistory.swift:7`) is `(target, tab)` plus three changeset-shaped
  fields. `AppStore.location(target:tab:)` (`:3671`) captures `.diff` as a bare `filePath` (dropping
  `source: DiffSource` and `change`, both needed to rebuild a `DiffDescriptor`) and captures `.file`
  as **nothing**.
- `applyLocation(_ loc:recordHistory:)` (`:3723`) bails at `guard let commitID = loc.commitID` — so
  **only changesets ever get content reinstated**. The recorded `.diff` `filePath` is dead data.

Chain: `⌘[` steps to an older entry that usually has the *same* `(target, tab)` pair → `focus()`
no-ops → the `commitID` guard returns → the pane is untouched, while `selectedTargetID`'s `didSet`
(`:156-177`) re-points the sidebar. The sidebar row highlight is a derived read of the focused tab
(`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:33`), so it tracks whatever content survives — which is why the
sidebar looks like it moved and the pane didn't.

Only the changeset path was ever wired end to end (`bc762c83`); diff and file tabs stayed on the old
`(target, tab)`-only contract. No test covers content replay: `AppStoreNavigationTests` is
terminal-tabs-only, `NavigationHistoryTests` is pure-value, no UI test drives back/forward.

Outcome: a history entry describes *what was on screen*, not just which tab, and replay reinstates it
for every content kind — so Back walks back through browsed diffs, files, commits, and in-commit file
selections.

## Governing rule (user, this session)

> **Back ignores anything that was closed. Nothing is ever reopened.**

Replay therefore **never creates a tab**. When a recorded location cannot be shown in a tab that
already exists, the entry is unreachable and Back **skips it** and keeps stepping. Retargeting the
shared preview slot is not "reopening" — that tab is open, and retargeting is exactly what browsing
does, which is what makes the core fix work.

## Approach

A recorded location becomes `(target, tab, identity, payload)`. Content mutation gets its own record
seam, because mutating a tab is not a focus change. Replay reinstates content through the existing
`openContentPreview` invariants — no new mutator, and no tab creation.

### 1. `Core/NavigationHistory.swift` — identity reuses `FocusedTabSelection`

`FocusedTabSelection` (`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:18-24`) is **already** the identity-only
reduction of a pane: `.changeset(commitID:)`, `.diff(path:source:)`, `.file(path:)`, terminal ⇒ `nil`.
It is already `Equatable`, and its doc already carries the "a new `TabContent` case has exactly one
site to teach" guarantee. Do not build a parallel enum — reuse it.

```swift
struct NavLocation: Equatable {
  let target: SidebarID
  let tab: TerminalTab.ID
  /// Identity: what makes two locations "the same place". `nil` ⇒ a terminal pane.
  let contentID: FocusedTabSelection?
  /// A changeset's in-commit file selection — identity too, because each selection is its own step.
  /// `FocusedTabSelection.changeset` deliberately carries only the commit id, so this rides alongside.
  let selectedPath: String?
  /// Replay payload — the full descriptor needed to re-open. EXCLUDED from `==`.
  let payload: NavPayload?

  static func == (l: Self, r: Self) -> Bool {
    l.target == r.target && l.tab == r.tab && l.contentID == r.contentID
      && l.selectedPath == r.selectedPath
  }
}

/// The replay payload. Three cases, not four: `TabContent.terminal` holds a live surface, which a
/// value-type history entry must never retain. A terminal location is `payload == nil`.
enum NavPayload { case diff(DiffDescriptor), file(FileDescriptor), changeset(ChangesetDescriptor) }
```

Splitting identity from payload is what removes the hand-written per-kind equality: the drifting
fields (`DiffDescriptor.change` on staging, `ChangesetDescriptor.title` reconstructed on replay,
`isPreview` on Keep Open) live only in `payload`, which `==` never reads — so `record`'s dedup can't
be defeated by drift, and a preview→persist flip is not a new step.

`record` / `step` / `maxEntries` unchanged. `prune(removing:)` unchanged — tab-keyed, so closing a tab
still drops its entries, per the governing rule. Add a doc comment stating the resulting asymmetry
(an entry naming a later-pinned tab survives that tab's close; one naming the preview slot dies with
it) and pin it with a test so it reads as deliberate.

### 2. `Core/TerminalSessions.swift` — one content-change seam, two fire sites

Content identity is mutated in exactly two places (`grep 'tab.content ='`): the retarget at `:410`
and `setChangesetSelectedPath` at `:525`. (`:473-479` is `persist` — `isPreview` only; `:980` is
terminal live state.) Fire the seam from **those two and nowhere else** — the other
`openContentPreview` / `openContentPersistent` branches all end in `setFocused` on a tab that wasn't
focused, so `onFocusChange` already records them. Firing from five sites would redefine the seam as
"an open happened" and ship a test for unreachable code.

- `var onTabContentChange: ((TerminalTarget.ID, TerminalTab.ID) -> Void)?` beside `onFocusChange`
  (`:198`), joining the existing `onTabsRemoved` / `onSurfaceFocused` callbacks.
- An `extension NavPayload` sited directly under `TabContent` (`:101-122`), so a fifth `TabContent`
  case is a compile error in one known place: `init?(_ content: TabContent)` (exhaustive, `isPreview`
  normalised to `false`, `.terminal` ⇒ `nil`), `matchesTab(_:) -> Bool` (delegates to each
  `ContentDescriptor.matches`), and `descriptor` for handing back to the openers.
- **Update the opener ASCII diagram at `:383-389`** to show that every arrow also records a step.
  Without it a reader adds a sixth opener and silently records nothing — this bug's failure mode.

### 3. `Core/AppStore.swift` — record centrally, replay without creating anything

- **`withHistorySuppressed(_:)`** — a save-and-reinstate-prior-value (or depth-counted) replacement
  for the bare `isNavigatingHistory = true; defer { … = false }` pairs at `:3703`, `:3728`, `:996`.
  Today those are two *sequential* windows, which happens to work; wrapping replay in one window
  would let the inner `applyLocation`'s `defer` clear the outer one and replay would record itself.
- **`location(target:tab:)`** (`:3671`) builds identity + payload from `tab.content` via one switch.
- **`applyLocation(_ loc:)`** (`:3723`) — one suppression window, ordered resolution, never creates a
  tab. Drop the dead `recordHistory` parameter (both callers pass `false`). Carries a new ASCII
  decision-tree diagram in its doc comment:

```
  applyLocation(loc)                       // never creates a tab (governing rule)
    │ select loc.target (project + target ids), guard live
    ├── contentID == nil  ─▶ terminal ─▶ focus loc.tab if it still exists ─▶ done
    └── contentID != nil  ─▶ payload must land in an EXISTING tab:
          ├─ 1. loc.tab exists AND payload.matchesTab(its content) ─▶ focus it
          ├─ 2. else some live tab matches payload                 ─▶ focus that tab
          ├─ 3. else the target has a preview slot                 ─▶ retarget it IN PLACE, focus it
          └─ 4. else                        UNREACHABLE ─▶ isLive already rejected it; Back skipped
        then, for the landed tab:
          ├─ .changeset ─▶ setChangesetSelectedPath(loc.selectedPath)
          └─ .diff      ─▶ re-resolve `change` from live status (see below)
```

- **`isLive(_:)`** (`:3746`) gains a content-reachability test, which is the mechanism behind
  "ignore what was closed" — `step(_:isLive:)` already skips entries the predicate rejects:

```swift
  // target alive && !missing, then:
  //   terminal entry  ⟺ loc.tab still exists
  //   content entry   ⟺ some tab matches the payload  ||  the target has a preview slot
```
  Synchronous and cheap — two dictionary walks, no VCS I/O. Deliberately does **not** ask whether the
  file or commit still exists on disk: that needs I/O inside a predicate run per candidate during
  `step`, and the pane already renders its own `.failed` state.

- **Re-resolve `DiffDescriptor.change` on replay.** `change` is not inert — `Views/DiffViewer.swift:157`
  paints it as a coloured letter and `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:293/872/878` gates "Open file in…"
  on `change == .deleted`. Writing a record-time value back would enable that menu item for a file
  that is gone. Look the path up in the live changed-file list the Changes panel already renders and
  use its current `change`; fall back to the recorded value when status isn't loaded yet.
  `DiffDescriptor` and its construction sites are untouched.

- **Wire `terminals.onTabContentChange`** in `init` beside `:828`, guarded on
  `!isNavigatingHistory` **and** `targetID == selectedTarget?.id` **and**
  `tabID == terminals.focusedTab(for: selected)?.id`, then `recordCurrentLocation()`.
  The `!isNavigatingHistory` check is mandatory: `recordCurrentLocation` (`:3661`) does **not**
  self-guard ("guarded at the call sites"), and every existing caller carries it. Do *not* duplicate
  `onFocusChange`'s `fileFind.close()` / `refreshSelectionHasTabs()` — this is not a focus change.

- **Delete** the explicit `recordCurrentLocation()` calls at `:3493`, `:3502`, `:3515` and their
  local guards.

### 4. `Views/ChangesetDetailView.swift:311` — kill a phantom step

`selectedPath` (`:28-32`) falls back to `changeset.files.first?.path` for *display*, so the first row
renders selected while `descriptor.selectedPath == nil`. Tapping it passes `selectChangesetFile`'s
`d.selectedPath != path` guard and records a step whose replay is visually identical. Compare the tap
against the **effective** selection. Pre-existing, same bug class.

### 5. `Views/TitlebarBars.swift:113-129`

Add `.accessibilityIdentifier("toolbar.navigateBack")` / `"toolbar.navigateForward"`, matching the
existing `toolbar.toggleSidebar` convention. The UI test does **not** drive them (see Verification).

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

| Existing | Used for | Rebuilt? |
|---|---|---|
| `FocusedTabSelection` (`Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:18`) | the location's content identity | **No** — reused; a parallel `NavContent` enum was designed and then deleted from this plan |
| `openContentPreview` invariants A/B/C (`TerminalSessions.swift:400`) | replay's dedup + in-place retarget | No — replay adds no mutator |
| `ContentDescriptor.matches` (`:136`), `sameFile`, `sameChangeset` | payload↔tab matching | No |
| `onFocusChange` / `onTabsRemoved` / `onSurfaceFocused` (`:198-209`) | the callback pattern the new seam follows | No |
| `history.prune` via `onTabsRemoved` (`AppStore.swift:843`) | closed-tab cleanup | No — unchanged |
| `setChangesetSelectedPath` (`:518`) | reinstating an in-commit file | No |
| `typeKey` UITest idiom (10+ files) + `Go ▸ Back` `⌘[` (`WorkroomApp.swift:1129`) | driving the E2E test | No |

## NOT in scope

| Deferred | Rationale |
|---|---|
| `activeInspectorSection` restore | → TODOS.md. Narrower than first thought: `ActivitySection.swift:43-46` stacks Changes + History + Pull Request in **one** pane, so diff↔commit needs no switch. Only Files↔Changes is affected, and only the sidebar list, never the pane. |
| Root-cause fix for stale `DiffDescriptor.change` | → TODOS.md. Replay is fixed here (§3); an ordinary open tab is still stale. Removing the field touches every construction site and three tab-strip sites — a separate refactor. |
| Deterministic tab lookup (`contentTab(matching:)` / `previewTabID` use `.first` over a Dictionary) | → TODOS.md. Latent pre-existing flakiness; `newPaneTab:689` deliberately bypasses dedup so ⌘D creates twins. Replay step 1 shields the common path. |
| Relaxing `prune`/`isLive` so content entries outlive their tab | Rejected by the governing rule: closed means ignored. |
| `diffViewModeOverride` / `markdownPreviewOverride` | View mode, not location. Retargeting preserves them anyway (they live on the tab, not the content). |
| Section collapse flags, inspector size weights, scroll offsets | Not part of a location. |

## Failure modes

| New codepath | Realistic production failure | Test? | Error handling? | Silent? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Replay resolution (§3) | Recorded content is in no tab and no preview slot exists → nothing to show | Yes — the inverted "never spawns, entry skipped" test | Yes — `isLive` rejects it, `step` skips | No: Back visibly moves further |
| Replay of a `.diff` whose file was reverted/deleted | `DiffResolver` finds nothing | Pane-level, not unit-testable | Yes — `DiffViewer` `.failed("Diff unavailable")` | No: pane states the failure |
| Replay of a `.changeset` whose commit is gone (rebase/abandon) | `VCSProviding.changeset` throws | Pane-level | Yes — `ChangesetDetailView` `.failed` (`:112`) | No |
| `change` re-resolution when status isn't loaded | Falls back to the recorded value | Yes | Yes — explicit fallback | No: worst case is today's badge |
| Nested `withHistorySuppressed` | Inner `defer` clears the outer window, replay records itself | Yes — "replay appends nothing" | Yes — save/reinstate | Would be silent; **that is why the test is mandatory** |
| Seam fires for a non-selected co-displayed target | Records a wrong-moment entry | Yes | Yes — the three-part guard | No |

**Critical gaps (no test AND no error handling AND silent): 0.**

## Parallelization

Sequential implementation, no parallelization opportunity. Steps 1-3 are three files in
`WorkroomApp/Core/` with a hard dependency chain (the type shape gates the seam, which gates the
replay wiring); steps 4-5 are two-line view edits. Splitting a ~150-line change across worktrees
costs more in merge coordination than it saves.

## Verification

**Existing tests that must change:** `WorkroomAppTests/NavigationHistoryTests.swift` only — `:52-59`
and `:68` construct `NavLocation(commitID:commitTitle:filePath:)`. Give the new fields defaults so
its `loc()` helper (`:11`) and every terminal-only test survive. `AppStoreNavigationTests.swift`
needs no changes (it reads only `.target` / `.tab`).

Adding files needs `xcodegen generate` — `make app-test` / `make app-uitest` run it, a direct
`xcodebuild` does not (`make app-generate` first).

**New pure tests** (`NavigationHistoryTests`): preview→persist normalisation dedups; changeset
`title` drift dedups; diff `change` drift dedups; `.diff` vs `.file` on the same path are distinct
steps; a changeset's `selectedPath` makes each in-commit selection its own step; `prune`'s
adjacent-dup collapse with content entries; the `prune` asymmetry (pinned-tab entry survives,
preview-tab entry dies).

**New store tests** (`AppStoreContentNavigationTests`), driving the real `store.openDiffPreview` /
`openFilePreview` / `openChangesetPreview` paths:

1. Two diff previews → 2 entries → `navigateBack()` shows the first diff **in the same tab id**, with
   `tabs(for:).count == 1`. **This is the reported bug.**
2. Diff → `.file` for the same path → Back shows the `.diff` (cross-kind retarget).
3. Preview-then-persist for the same file records exactly one entry.
4. Keep Open, browse away with a preview slot still available, Back → pinned tab unchanged, content
   lands in the preview slot.
5. **Replay never creates a tab:** pin every tab so no preview slot exists, then Back → the entry is
   skipped, `tabs(for:).count` unchanged, and the cursor lands on the next reachable entry.
6. ⌘D twin panes (same content, two tab ids) → Back to the anchor's entry focuses the **anchor**
   (step 1 prefers the recorded tab), tab count unchanged.
7. Changeset `selectedPath` reinstated across Back and Forward.
8. Replay appends nothing across a diff/changeset sequence (nested-suppression regression).
9. A content change in a non-selected co-displayed target records nothing.
10. `closeTab` on the browse preview prunes its entries and `canGoBack` goes honest.
11. Cross-workroom Back that also reinstates content (workroom switch + content restore in one call).
12. Terminal ↔ content transition: focus a terminal, open a diff, Back → the terminal pane.
13. Replayed `.diff` re-resolves `change` from live status; falls back to the recorded value when
    status is empty.

**New sessions tests** (`TerminalSessionsTests`): the seam fires on the preview retarget with the
retargeted tab id; fires on `setChangesetSelectedPath`; does **not** fire on `persist` /
`setDiffViewMode` / `setMarkdownPreview`; does **not** fire on the spawn or dedup branches (those
record via `onFocusChange`).

**One XCUITest** — `WorkroomAppUITests/NavigationHistoryContentUITests.swift` (new file ⇒ needs
`xcodegen generate`), fixture mode, Changes panel. **Drive Back with the keystroke**, not the
chevron: `app.typeKey("[", modifierFlags: .command)` is the idiom in 10+ existing UI tests, `Go ▸
Back` already owns `⌘[` (`WorkroomApp.swift:1129`) and it is reserved from the terminal via
`isAppShortcut`. Zero UI tests have ever driven a `toolbar.*` titlebar-accessory identifier, and a tap
that hits nothing there fails **silently** — a green test proving nothing.

The fixture already seeds distinct working-copy rows (`UITestFixture.swift:633-638`: `Gemfile`,
`app/models/user.rb`, `config/routes.rb`). Click `changes.file.Gemfile` → await
`terminal.tab.Gemfile`; click `changes.file.app/models/user.rb` → await `terminal.tab.user.rb` and
assert `terminal.tab.Gemfile` is **gone** (proves in-place retarget); `⌘[` → assert the chip is back,
**the pane's text contains "Gemfile"** (the pane is the actual bug — the chip alone doesn't prove it),
and the pane count is still 1; `⌘]` → `user.rb`.

```
cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj \
  -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData \
  -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' \
  -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/NavigationHistoryContentUITests/testBackShowsPreviousDiffInThePane test
```

**Gate:** `make app-format`, `make app-lint`, `make app-test` — read pass/fail from the `.xcresult`
via `xcresulttool` (Xcode 26 hides the summary). `make app-*` needs the command sandbox disabled.

**Manual check** via `make app-run`: Changes panel, single-click three files, `⌘[` three times — the
pane must walk back file by file. Repeat in History with commits, and with a file selected inside a
changeset.

## Implementation Tasks

Synthesized from this review's findings. Each task derives from a specific finding above.

- [ ] **T1 (P1, human: ~3h / CC: ~15min)** — `Core/NavigationHistory.swift` — Make a location
  `(target, tab, contentID, selectedPath, payload)`, identity reusing `FocusedTabSelection`
  - Surfaced by: cross-model tension 5 — `FocusedTabSelection:18-24` already is this identity type
  - Files: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/NavigationHistory.swift`
  - Verify: `make app-test` (`NavigationHistoryTests`)
- [ ] **T2 (P1, human: ~2h / CC: ~10min)** — `Core/TerminalSessions.swift` — Add
  `onTabContentChange`, fire from exactly the retarget (`:410`) and `setChangesetSelectedPath`
  (`:518`); add the `NavPayload` bridge under `TabContent`
  - Surfaced by: root cause — a content mutation is not a focus change; finding 7 — 3 of 5 fire sites are dead
  - Files: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift`
  - Verify: `make app-test` (`TerminalSessionsTests`)
- [ ] **T3 (P1, human: ~4h / CC: ~20min)** — `Core/AppStore.swift` — `withHistorySuppressed`,
  content-aware `isLive`, ordered replay that never creates a tab, seam wiring with the
  `!isNavigatingHistory` guard, delete the three explicit record calls
  - Surfaced by: root cause (`:3725` guard) + governing rule + outside voice §8 (missing guard)
  - Files: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift`
  - Verify: `make app-test` (`AppStoreContentNavigationTests`)

26	- [libghostty run exit code zero](libghostty-run-exit-code-zero.md) — GhosttyKit 1.2.3 reports run child exit_code as 0 always; capture real `$?` via an EXIT-trap wrapper `.exit` file; only XCUITest catches the gap.

29	- [macapp XCUITest gotchas](macapp-xcuitest-gotchas.md) — `.onHover` controls not drivable; a11y id on an NSViewRepresentable wrapper not queryable; assert PlainFileViewer content via `app.textViews` `value CONTAINS` (scoped, not `.any`).
30	- [macapp Settings/aux window gotchas](macapp-settings-aux-window-gotchas.md) — Settings/About are separate Scenes: theme via event-driven re-apply (static view → rare updateNSView → white titlebar flicker), ⌘W shadowed by "Close Terminal" (close via WindowRegistry.store(for:)==nil), `@Default` invalidates SwiftUI ASYNC (use @State for click-immediate UI), XCUITest can't match Form Toggle by label (use a11y id).
31	- [VCS foundation: Rust core](vcs-foundation-rust-core.md) — Workroom pivoting to VCS/code IDE; issue #59 first brick; HYBRID foundation: jj→Rust jj-lib/UniFFI, git→SwiftGitX (gix dropped), unified at Swift VCSProviding; Phase-0 proven live + committed in `vcs/`.
32	- [UI tests for macapp features](ui-tests-for-macapp-features.md) — Joel wants XCUITest coverage for new macapp UI (panels/tabs/interactions), not just unit tests; mind the XCUITest gotchas + use the UITestFixture seam.
33	- [macapp UI tests: scope to the changed methods](macapp-uitest-only-relevant-class.md) — never run the full `WorkroomAppUITests` suite (too slow); `make app-uitest` IGNORES `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so call `xcodebuild` directly with `-only-testing:<Class>/<method>`; they live in their own scheme.
34	- [Contrast metric was not WCAG](contrast-metric-not-wcag.md) — `ThemeTokens.luminance` skipped sRGB linearization, so 38 of 56 themes lost the rail's Liquid Glass; fixed app-wide, `perceivedBrightness` keeps light/dark detection, ink now measured not thresholded.
35	- [UserDefaults ignores a throwaway $HOME](userdefaults-not-isolated-by-home.md) — cfprefsd resolves the real home, so QA isolates `~/.config/workroom` but never `Defaults`-backed state (theme, inspector, channel).
36	- [mask + contentShape preserves hits](macapp-mask-contentshape-preserves-hits.md) — `.mask` + `.contentShape(.interaction, Rectangle())` DOES keep descendant hit-testing (verified, real mouse); test MID-scroll or `contentMargins` hides the ramp.
37	- [macapp DiffViewer .task re-fire loop](macapp-diffviewer-task-refire-loop.md) — the "history file diff just shows the loader" bug = a SwiftUI .task re-fire loop; fixed with a load-once-per-file loadedKey guard.
38	- [macapp CLI shell-out cooperative pool](macapp-cli-shellout-cooperative-pool.md) — VCS `jj` CLI shell-outs must block on GCD not the Swift cooperative pool (a latent concurrent-read starvation risk; NOT the loader bug).
39	- [VCS foundation toolchain](vcs-foundation-toolchain.md) — build gotchas: protoc required; Homebrew rust can't cross x86_64 (rustup for universal); jj-lib read pattern (no wc lock); UniFFI library-mode bindgen from vcs/; static-Rust link needs no native-lib flags; SwiftGitX API; library-only-xcframework + C-module-target trick to avoid the GhosttyKit modulemap collision.
40	- [jj native status needs snapshot](jj-native-status-needs-snapshot.md) — a jj-lib-native working-copy STATUS read must snapshot (take the WC lock + rewrite @), unlike read-only log/changeset; model on jayjay's refresh_working_copy; corruption risk, test on throwaway repos; CLI resolveJJ stays the correct impl meanwhile.

42	- [History loads forever → GCD](macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd.md) — History pane spinner-forever (fixed by tab-switch) = its blocking log read starved on the cooperative pool by the status-snapshot burst; fixed via `runBlocking` (GCD) + synchronous `VCSProviding.log`.

47	- [SCK own-process capture needs no TCC](sck-own-process-capture-no-tcc.md) — measured: own-window capture works with preflight=false, no prompt, non-key window fine; but `filter.contentRect` ≠ `NSWindow.frame` (y-down, ~5pt inset) so deriving scale from the frame drifts ~1.2%.
48	- [Borderless panel casts no shadow](macapp-borderless-panel-no-shadow.md) — `hasShadow` is dead on a borderless non-opaque NSPanel (measured); draw it, mount it AFTER `clipShape`, and only a SwiftUI shape's shadow renders — a layer `shadowPath` doesn't.
